title: Northwest Airlink 2268
summary: Northwest Airlink Flight 2268, a CASA C-212 turboprop, was cleared for a visual approach to Runway 21R at Detroit Metropolitan Airport at 2:30 PM on March 4, 1987. At 60-70 feet above ground, the aircraft banked left and then rolled right, striking the ramp area inside and to the left of the runway threshold, flipping over and striking a catering truck before bursting into flames. The NTSB determined the probable cause was the captain's inability to recover from an asymmetric power condition at low speed following his intentional use of beta mode to descend and slow the aircraft rapidly on final approach. Nine of the 19 people on board were killed.
probable_cause: The National Transportation Safety Board determined the probable cause was the captain's inability to control the airplane in an attempt to recover from an asymmetric power condition at low speed following his intentional use of the beta mode of propeller operation to descend and slow the airplane rapidly on final approach. Contributing factors included unstabilized visual approach, a departing DC-9 on the runway, the desire to make a short field landing, higher-than-normal flight idle fuel flow settings on both engines, and the lack of fire-blocking material in passenger seat cushions which contributed to injury severity.

Descended below the minimum safe altitude until impact with the trees.
Aircraft crashed into forest in commune of Eysines in department of Gironde.

title: Finnair 915 missile explosion incident
summary: On 23 December 1987, Finnair Flight 915, a DC-10 with 201 passengers and 19 crew en route from Tokyo to Helsinki, was flying at cruise altitude of 10,600 m over the North Pole when the crew allegedly witnessed a missile explosion less than 30 seconds before what would have been impact. The aircraft continued to Helsinki and landed safely. The incident was not officially reported at the time, only becoming public in 2014 when Finnish media published pilot accounts comparing it to the 1983 Korean Air Lines Flight 007 shootdown. Investigation found that Finlandization prevented government action and the Civil Aviation Administration showed little interest in the matter.
probable_cause: Soviet missile allegedly fired by the Union as claimed by pilots Kaukiainen and another crew member, though never confirmed or officially investigated due to the incident not being reported at the time.

factors.evidence: Soviet Union had fired a missile at the aircraft, which exploded less than 30 seconds before impact according to pilot Kaukiainen
pilots had agreed that the pilot in command would file a report after the flight as his duty but he never did it, due in part to Christmas celebrations interfering
within the Finnish government there was little interest in the matter, Finnish Transport Safety Agency had no knowledge of the matter, because officials were damned Finlandized
aircraft continued safely to destination Helsinki after the alleged missile incident with no structural damage or injuries
